implementation_notes: Since Java 16 a `record` is the parameter object: a compact declaration whose components become private final fields, a canonical constructor, accessor methods and generated `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString`, replacing the classic POJO with constructor, getters and IDE-generated equality. Invariants go in a compact canonical constructor, and mutable components must be defensively copied there because records are only shallowly immutable.
pitfalls: Records are only shallowly immutable: a `List` or array component can still be mutated by callers - copy it in the compact constructor.
Records cannot extend a class and have no no-argument constructor, so frameworks that need bean-style construction (JPA entities, some serializers) cannot use them directly.
A record with many components reintroduces positional construction; use named static factory methods or a builder as the group grows.

variants.name: Final-field class with getters (Java 8)
variants.implementation_notes: The pre-record form: a small final class with private final fields, a constructor that validates, accessor methods and equals/hashCode/toString written by the IDE or a tool such as Lombok. It is still the correct choice on Java 8-15 toolchains and for carriers that a framework must instantiate or proxy; the record variant removes the boilerplate entirely where the toolchain allows.
pitfalls: Hand-maintained equals/hashCode drift from the fields as the group grows - regenerate or use a tool.
Setters or non-final fields make the carrier mutable and reintroduce the aliasing the parameter object was meant to remove.
Carrier classes that outgrow their users tend to be promoted into their own package prematurely; a static nested class is often enough.
